questions.q: What are the three building blocks every flow is made of?
questions.explain: Every flow is built from elements (nodes), connectors (lines defining order), and resources (referenced containers).

questions.q: Which element category does the Decision and Loop element belong to?
questions.explain: Decision and Loop are Logic elements — they interact with the flow itself, not with users or Salesforce records directly.

questions.q: Why does a flow still need a Data element or Action even after using Logic elements to change a value?
options: Logic elements are always slower than Data elements
Logic elements can only run once per flow
Logic elements only change data inside the running flow — nothing persists without a Data element or Action
Logic elements require a screen to display their output
questions.explain: Logic operates only within the flow; to make a change stick after the flow finishes, a Data element or Action is required.

questions.q: Where in Flow Builder do you create a new resource like a variable?
options: The New Resource button in the Toolbox
The canvas's plus (+) icon between elements
questions.explain: Resources are created from the New Resource button in the Toolbox panel, not as nodes on the canvas.

questions.q: Which Interaction element calls another, already-built autolaunched flow from inside the current flow?
questions.explain: Subflow is the Interaction element that calls another autolaunched flow; it's covered in depth in Lesson 11.
